paragraphs: Rabbi Elazar son of Tzadok. See the earlier tannaitic entry. Lulav va-Aravah: apparently an amora, since Ivo and Chizkiyah, Rav’s daughter’s sons, were before him. False testimony: they were before Rav; Rav’s father Ivo was before Elazar son of Tzadok, Sukkah 44b. “Likewise they said from Shmuel: he walked three parasangs on Friday” should read “in his name: one should not walk more than three parasangs on a Friday.” After several amora names, Yuchasin lists Elazar son of Yitzchak, with Ivo and Chizkiyah, Rav’s daughter’s sons, and Ivo reading before him. Confused: they were before Elazar son of Tzadok, as he wrote above; thus errors. In fact Elazar son of Yitzchak appears nowhere in the Talmud except Horayot 13b, itself erroneous, since immediately the same matter is in Tzadok’s son’s name. There is Elazar bar Yitzchak of Kefar Darom below, apparently early, in Yishmael’s time.
